summary: After Saul rejected, Yahweh says to Samuel how long will you mourn for Saul, fill horn with oil go to Jesse Bethlehemite I have provided me a king among his sons. Samuel fears Saul will kill, Yahweh says say I come to sacrifice, invite Jesse. Jesse makes sons pass: Eliab looks kingly, Yahweh says don't look on appearance or height, man looks outward, Yahweh looks on heart. Seven sons pass, none chosen, Samuel says are all here? There remains youngest keeping sheep. Send fetch, he was ruddy with beautiful eyes and goodly, Yahweh says arise anoint him, Samuel anoints in midst of brothers, Spirit of Yahweh came on David from that day forward. Later Saul tormented by evil spirit, servants seek musician, one says son of Jesse cunning in playing, mighty man, etc, Saul sends for David, loves him, made armor-bearer, whenever evil spirit on Saul David plays harp and Saul refreshed.
whyItMatters: Classic God looks on heart not appearance — David, youngest shepherd, overlooked, anointed. Contrasts Saul's height and appearance with David's heart. Also Spirit comes on David as leaves Saul — transfer of kingship.

outline.heading: Samuel mourns Saul, sent to Jesse Bethlehem to anoint among sons
Seven sons pass, don't look on outward, Yahweh looks on heart
Youngest keeping sheep — ruddy, beautiful, anointed, Spirit came
Saul tormented, seeks harpist, David cunning in playing, loves him, refreshes

keyVerses.text: But Yahweh said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but Yahweh looks at the heart.”
Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the middle of his brothers. Then Yahweh’s Spirit came mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up and went to Ramah.
keyVerses.why: Spirit transfer — came on David as departed from Saul.

themes: man looks outward Yahweh looks on heart

questions.question: Why does God say man looks outward but Yahweh looks on heart? Is this anti-appearance?
questions.answer: Eliab is tall, impressive like Saul was (Saul taller than all). Samuel assumes. God corrects: don't look on face or height, I have rejected him. Man sees eyes, Yahweh sees heart (leb — inner orientation, not just emotion). Not that appearance irrelevant, but God sees inner truth Eliab lacks (later Eliab angry at David in ch 17). David's heart here is described as after God's heart later, though flawed.

questions.question: Why youngest keeping sheep, not at feast?
questions.answer: Seven sons at sacrifice, youngest not invited initially — shepherding is lowly, youth. Jesse doesn't even consider him candidate. Samuel must ask are all here? There remains youngest (haqqaton) — diminutive. Like Joseph and David as shepherds, overlooked. God chooses unlikely, young, shepherd — pattern of God looking beyond human ranking.

questions.question: What does Spirit came mightily on David from that day forward vs left Saul mean?
questions.answer: In Old Testament, Spirit comes upon judges, kings for task empowerment, not necessarily permanent indwelling as in New Testament. Spirit rushing on David marks kingship empowerment; the Spirit departed from Saul (16:14) marks rejection. David will still sin (Bathsheba), but Spirit remains for calling. Foreshadows new covenant where Spirit given to all, not just king.

questions.question: Why does Saul need harp and David playing refreshes him?
questions.answer: Saul tormented by evil (perhaps harmful) spirit from Yahweh — distress, paranoia after rejection. Servants suggest seek man cunning in playing lyre. David described as cunning, mighty man, man of war, judicious, handsome, Yahweh with him — resume. Music as therapy — David plays, Saul refreshed, well, evil spirit departs. Shows David's art soothes where Saul's kingship fails, and brings David into court to see kingship.

glossary.term: man looks outward Yahweh looks on heart
glossary.def: Appearance vs inner orientation — central principle in David choice.
Rushed, seized — empowerment for kingship task.
